Domain audited for this task: the extended policies `guestplan_ext_level_election_cover` and `guestplan_ext_protection_fee_assessment`, together with every base policy governing their subjects — `guestplan_evt_fee_charging` (subject `guestplan_protection_fee_charged`), `guestplan_election_eligibility` and `guestplan_agg_claim_history` (subject `guestplan_election_confirmed`) — the whole variant table they read, every untriggered branch, the retired surface, and the task-tool contracts.

## source_to_kb

### Base policy `guestplan_election_eligibility`

All six rule sentences are carried in `election_eligibility_terms_0b9e34c7`, in order and at the same strength: the minimum age and minimum score read on the day the trip starts and the quoting of the levels the guest does qualify for; the exclusion ceiling and the excluded value classes; declining protection only on evidence of the guest's own motor policy at the level's minimum third-party limit, with "the guest's word that they are insured is not evidence of it"; commercial carriage and cross-border trips covered only on the levels that say so; a level choosable only for a trip confirmed and not yet started; additional drivers approved up to the level's maximum and not covered if unapproved before the trip starts.

Both eligibility contracts are carried in the "Where the evidence must come from" section: `own_policy_evidenced` (authority `system_record`, timing `pre_action`, correlation `guestplan_elections.election_id`) as "the insurer standing on the election record, together with the election reference and the level recorded on it, is what the marketplace reads before the level is taken"; and `trip_confirmed_not_started` (state_contract `trips_bookings.status ∈ [booked]`) as "The trip beneath the election must stand as booked on the Keyturn Trip Booking record correlated by the booking reference, read before the level is taken." Per-tier params live in `driver_admission_terms_b41d9e05` (age, score, driver counts and fees, own-policy switch and minimum limit, international licence) and `vehicle_and_trip_limits_9a2ce7f4` (longest trip, value ceiling, excluded classes, the three journey switches), each across all six levels. No sentence retired and none added.

All four rule sentences carried in `claim_history_and_days_read_together_41fc9a0b`, including the suspension count, the waiting period counted in whole calendar days from the day the last loss was settled, "A guest barred from one level may still elect a lower one", and the forward-quoting rule "a guest whose covered days would take one trip past the level's maximum trip length is quoted on the level that will carry the whole trip rather than on one that would run out midway". Per-tier params (`suspension_after_claims_count`, `reinstatement_wait_days`, `annual_claim_limit_count`, `maximum_trip_days_covered`) in `claim_limits_and_suspension_terms_af13d6e2` and `vehicle_and_trip_limits_9a2ce7f4`, all six levels.

### Extended policy `guestplan_ext_level_election_cover`

`baseline.rule` is carried complete across the hub and the computation document: the settling sentence ("When a guest settles the protection that will run on a trip, the marketplace fixes at the same time how many days of cover the election will carry, so that the guest is told which day cover ends on rather than discovering it at a claim") in `settling_protection_for_a_trip_0c48ea77`, and the measure ("the reserved hours of the trip divided by the hours in a day and rounded up to a whole day, never fewer than the minimum cover days, and never more than the cover ceiling") in `days_of_cover_an_election_carries_b6d1f28c`. `baseline.params` are all three rendered: "The hours in a day are 24. The minimum cover days are 1. The cover ceiling is 30 days." The baseline's order is carried explicitly ("The reserved hours are divided by the hours in a day first and the result carried up to the next whole day; the figure so reached is then raised to the minimum cover days if it falls below them, and finally held down to the cover ceiling if it stands above it").

## kb_to_source

Every normative claim in the two hubs, the two computation documents, the nine factor documents and the base-policy documents in this task's domain was traced to a source sentence, a `params` value, an `eligibility` contract, a `lifecycle` transition or a task-tool contract. The scans reported in the task 0 file were run over the same corpus and return the same result: no added confirmation, review, notification or exception procedure; no cross-problem operational guidance; no task world state written in as a policy fact (the worked ledgers in `loyalty_rate_on_the_protection_fee_9f2071ab` — six trips and an overage five months ago — and in `late_return_allowance_on_cover_e281c034` — three late returns — are not this guest's rows, which are three trips with no overage in the window and two late returns). The guest-only character of the settlement ("Only the guest decides what their own cover will be, so the marketplace does not settle a level on their behalf") restates `lifecycle.transitions`: `{from: quoted, to: elected, by: user, means: The guest chooses a protection level for the trip, which only the guest can do.}` — not an addition.

Three things the documents state, or fail to state, that do not match the source:

- **B1** — a retired clause restated as in force (below).
- **B2** — a factor document attributing the clamp to the wrong ceiling (below).
- **B3** — the assembly order of the loyalty rate and the long-stay discount, which the source states and no document carries (below).

## bijection_verdict

**KB-BIJECTION RED**, on three related findings, which together leave this task's scored fee under-determined on the visible surface.

### B1 — a retired clause of `guestplan_evt_fee_charging` is still stated as a rule in force

- *Symptom*: the corpus asserts that the ceiling recorded against a level is the most the protection fee may come to for one trip.
- *Root cause*: the schedule document frames its "Ceiling recorded (USD)" column normatively, unlike its neighbouring descriptions and unlike its own later heading.
- *Evidence*:
  - `protection_fee_schedule_7c1a4b93`, opening paragraph: "…the floor is the least the fee may come to for one trip and **the ceiling recorded against the level the most**; the billing point is the point recorded against the level…"
  - source `guestplan_ext_protection_fee_assessment.overwrite[2].superseded_clause`: "The fee arrived at is then held between the level's floor and its ceiling, the floor applied first and the ceiling last, so a trip long enough to pass the ceiling pays the ceiling and no more."
  - the same clause is correctly written as retired in `protection_fee_charging_basis_e92b7150`, "Clauses no longer in force" item 5 — so the corpus contradicts itself.
  - the figures put in force by the sentence (950.00 / 1600.00 / 2400.00 / 3600.00 / 5200.00) are not the figures in force (1200.00 / 2400.00 / 3200.00, by length of reservation, per `ceiling_on_the_protection_fee_for_one_trip_c7196e3f`).
- *Affected document and location*: `docs/guestplan/protection_fee_schedule_7c1a4b93.json`, first paragraph.
- *Bearing*: on this task's world the level in force is Keyturn Advantage Protection, whose recorded ceiling is 2400.00 USD, below the 3182.025 the fee reaches. A reader who follows this sentence scores 2490.00 instead of 3272.03.

### B2 — a factor document attributes the clamp to the level's ceiling rather than the one in force

- *Symptom*: the document that pins the mileage step's position names the ceiling it comes after with a possessive whose antecedent is the level.
- *Root cause*: the source's assembly sentence says "held at the level's floor and then under **the trip ceiling that applies**" — two different owners, the floor being the level's and the ceiling the reservation's. The rendering collapsed them onto one owner.
- *Evidence*:
  - `mileage_exposure_step_on_the_fee_6ad0f4b2`: "The step is added after the fee has been held at **the level's** floor and under **its** ceiling, and the step itself is not held down by that ceiling."
  - source `guestplan_ext_protection_fee_assessment.overwrite[2].replaced_by`: "…held at the level's floor and then under the trip ceiling that applies, with the mileage step added to that figure…"
  - the baseline document names the right one — `protection_fee_for_a_trip_1c6d80fa`: "held at the level's floor and then under **the ceiling on the protection fee for one trip**, which is 1200.00 USD".
- *Affected document and location*: `docs/guestplan/mileage_exposure_step_on_the_fee_6ad0f4b2.json`, paragraph beginning "The step is added after".
- *Bearing*: read together with B1 it makes the wrong ceiling the natural one, giving 2490.00.

### B3 — the assembly order of the loyalty rate and the long-stay discount is an atom of the source with no home in any document

- *Symptom*: the visible corpus does not say whether the loyalty rate and the long-stay discount are taken before or after the fee is held at the floor and under the ceiling, and on this task's figures the two orders give different numbers.
- *Root cause*: the source fixes the order in the extended policy's assembly sentence, which is both the closing line of its `rule` and the `replaced_by` of its third `overwrite`. That sentence names the loyalty rate, the long-stay discount and the mileage step, so it cannot be rendered in the baseline computation document without disclosing that those variations exist; and the render homed the positional information for only one of the three, leaving the other two unplaced. The same policy's siblings show the gap is avoidable: `guestplan_ext_additional_driver_charge` homes its assembly's proportion inside its seat-days factor document ("what is taken is the level's additional driver fee in the proportion the seat days bear to the covered days"), and `guestplan_ext_young_driver_surcharge` homes its assembly's position inside its trip-step factor document ("added after the surcharge has been held to its ceiling").
- *Evidence*:
  - source `guestplan_ext_protection_fee_assessment.rule`, closing sentence, and `overwrite[2].replaced_by`: "The protection fee for a trip is therefore the fee the level's basis produces for the charged days, **taken at the loyalty rate and then reduced by the long-stay discount, held at the level's floor and then under the trip ceiling that applies**, with the mileage step added to that figure, and the whole rounded to two decimal places at the end."
  - source `compute`: `discounted_fee: "base_fee * loyalty_fee_rate * (1 - stay_discount_rate / 100)"`, `result: "RND(MN(MX(discounted_fee, level_floor), trip_fee_ceiling) + mileage_step, 2)"`.
  - the baseline document `protection_fee_for_a_trip_1c6d80fa` states a complete ordered pipeline with no slot for either: "The charged days are settled first… The level's daily amount is then taken for each of those charged days. The figure so reached is raised to the level's floor if it stands below it, and only then held down to 1200.00 USD if it stands above that; the whole is rounded to two decimal places at the end."
  - `long_stay_discount_on_the_protection_fee_3b84cc17` says only "A long-stay discount is taken off the protection fee of a Keyturn Guest Protection Plan election… the stay discount rate of the figure it is taken off" — position unstated.
  - `loyalty_rate_on_the_protection_fee_9f2071ab` says only "The loyalty rate is the share of the protection fee a guest with a record on the marketplace is asked for" — position unstated.
- *Affected documents and locations*: the omission is corpus-wide; the documents where the semantics would have to live are `long_stay_discount_on_the_protection_fee_3b84cc17` and `loyalty_rate_on_the_protection_fee_9f2071ab` (each silent on its own position), read against `protection_fee_for_a_trip_1c6d80fa`.
- *Bearing*: decisive. On this task's inputs the basis produces 3806.25, which stands above the 3200.00 ceiling in force, so the order changes the answer: the source's order gives **3272.03**; clamping first gives **2765.20**; and with B1/B2 clamping at the level's recorded 2400.00 gives **2490.00**.

Relation to previous revisions: none; revision 1. The policy-side audit under `audits/policy_task/guest_protection_desk/` was not read before the blind answer was frozen and is not relied on here.

Everything else in this task's domain corresponds losslessly at the level of entailment: both `baseline.rule`s complete with their default constants and their stated order, all nine factor ladders complete tier by tier with thresholds in figures and compound conditions intact, the prerequisite sentence verbatim on its blocked side and in no other policy's document, the three base policies governing the subjects carried whole with their eligibility contracts, and the retired surface otherwise correct.

### B1, B2, B3 — all three closed

- **B1 — closed.** The schedule's framing sentence now reads "the floor is the least the fee may come to for one trip; **the ceiling recorded and the billing point recorded are the terms of those names standing against the level**". The ceiling has been moved across the clause boundary to join the billing point — the charter's other retired term — while the floor keeps its normative predicate, which is correct because the floor is in force and the ceiling is not. All six recorded ceilings remain carried as values, so the retired clause still has a bearing document and is written there as retired rather than deleted. Verified against `guestplan_ext_protection_fee_assessment.overwrite[2]`.
- **B2 — closed.** `mileage_exposure_step_on_the_fee_6ad0f4b2` now says "held at the level's floor and then under **the trip ceiling that applies**", matching the charter's assembly sentence word for word on the ownership of each bound. The possessive that pointed at the retired per-level ceiling is gone.
- **B3 — closed, and the uniqueness was verified blind before the reveal.** Both multipliers now carry their own positional clause, in the factor document that renders each, exactly as the two sibling policies already did. Reading the published corpus alone, the pipeline is fully ordered — charged days, the level's basis, the loyalty rate, the long-stay discount, the level's floor, the trip ceiling, the mileage step, then rounding half up to the cent — and it yields **one** number, 3238.53. The two readings revision 1 could not exclude are now excluded by quoted sentences, and each was computed so the exclusion is not a matter of taste: clamp-first would give 2737.04, the level's-recorded-ceiling reading 2075.28. The reveal confirms the derived order is the charter's `result = RND(MN(MX(base_fee × loyalty_fee_rate × (1 − stay_discount_rate/100), level_floor), trip_fee_ceiling) + mileage_step, 2)`. Separately, and not inferred from that agreement, the rounding point was checked in exact rational arithmetic: 3806.25 × 94/100 × 88/100 = 3148.53 **exactly**, so the final figure is 323853 hundredths with fractional part zero and there is nothing for a rounding convention to decide.
- **Baselines stayed silent, as claimed.** Swept mechanically: neither `protection_fee_for_a_trip_1c6d80fa` nor `days_of_cover_an_election_carries_b6d1f28c` contains "unless", "adjustment", "may apply", "except", "set out elsewhere", "certain customers", "qualify for", "otherwise provided", or the business name of any factor in the product. The positional information lives entirely in the factor documents, so a reader of the baseline still learns nothing about what modifies it.

### bijection_verdict (revision 2)

**PASS.** All three revision-1 findings are closed, no atom of this task's domain is unborne or borne with changed meaning, and the rework introduced no claim from outside the source.

### dependency_form (revision 2)

**PASS.** Re-run over the republished corpus: the prerequisite sentence still verbatim in `charging_the_protection_fee_ae52c3d9` and in exactly one file across `docs/`; the five tool identifiers still one per own hub; no aggregated chain, no route, no cross-problem guidance, no task-mirroring title; the depended-on document still discloses nothing about who waits on it.

One sentence required judgement and is recorded as a policy-side note rather than a verdict, for the reason revision 1 gave when it met the base state clause in `protection_fee_charging_basis_e92b7150`: a sentence rendered as its source has it is not something the rendering added.

### P2 — policy-side note: the charter put a cross-factor reference inside a factor's own rule text

`long_stay_discount_on_the_protection_fee_3b84cc17` says its discount "is taken off **after the loyalty rate has been applied** and before the fee is held at the level's floor or under the trip ceiling". A sweep of all 51 documents for the business name of every factor in the product shows this is the **only** document in the corpus that names a factor other than the one it renders; every other factor document names only its own quantity, and where it pins a slot it names baseline elements alone ("the level's floor", "the trip ceiling", "the ceiling on the loading for one trip", "the cost of the level moved to").

The sentence is a verbatim carriage of `guestplan_ext_protection_fee_assessment.rule`, so the renderer is faithful and the fault is not the rendering's. But the effect on the corpus is real and worth stating: a solver who reaches the long-stay discount from the trip's reserved period is told, without having looked at any record, that a loyalty rate exists — which is the one thing the discrete topology of computation and factor documents is meant to withhold, the existence of a factor being something the reader is supposed to discover from the customer's own records.

Two things make this narrow rather than serious. It discloses the existence of one sibling factor inside one computation; it hands over no tool, no route, no chain between problems and no hop of the problem tree. And the clause is **normatively inert**: the loyalty rate and the long-stay discount are both multipliers, so their order relative to each other cannot change any figure, and the load-bearing half of the sentence — "before the fee is held at the level's floor or under the trip ceiling" — stands on its own without naming anything. The semantics the corpus must entail would survive the clause's removal from the charter's rule text, which is what makes it reportable. Where it belongs, and what should be done about it, is not mine to design.
